edges.limitations: The inheritance does not match. MENX is recessive and the affected rats are homozygous, whereas human MEN4 is dominant and patients are heterozygous. The rat therefore models near-complete p27 loss rather than the reduced-dosage state that the human entry's trunk is built on, which is the mechanism most in question.

nodes.description: Anterior pituitary adenomas occur in a substantial minority, at a median age of about 39 years with a reported range from 5 to 79 years. About three-quarters are hormone-secreting - corticotroph, lactotroph and somatotroph lesions - and the remainder nonfunctioning. Germline CDKN1B loss of function is also a recognised cause of paediatric Cushing disease, with or without the wider MEN4 phenotype, which is the main reason this syndrome reaches paediatric practice.

nodes.description: Expansion occurs in hormone-producing endocrine lineages, giving a monoclonal adenoma whose parent cell still secretes. Parathyroid chief cells are the commonest lineage and corticotrophs, somatotrophs and lactotrophs the next; pancreatic and enteroendocrine lineages account for the neuroendocrine tumours. Because the adenoma retains the secretory programme of its parent cell, the clinical picture is autonomous hormone output rather than mass effect alone.

nodes.description: A germline heterozygous loss-of-function variant in CDKN1B is present in every cell. Reported routes to reduced protein include nonsense and frameshift alleles, missense changes that accelerate proteasomal turnover or mislocalise the protein out of the nucleus, and non-coding variants in the 5-prime untranslated region that disrupt an upstream open reading frame and lower translational reinitiation at the CDKN1B start codon.

nodes.description: MENX is a spontaneous multiple endocrine neoplasia-like syndrome in the rat, and it is where this disease was found. Mapping the MENX locus identified a homozygous Cdkn1b frameshift, and that result is what prompted the search for a germline CDKN1B variant in MEN1-mutation-negative patients. The model is therefore not a post-hoc recapitulation but the origin of the gene-disease hypothesis.

nodes.description: The cardinal manifestation and the first in most patients, presenting as hypercalcaemia from autonomous parathyroid hormone secretion. It is usually uniglandular (86% single adenoma) and recurs in only about 6%, both of which distinguish it from the multiglandular, recurrence-prone hyperparathyroidism of MEN1. Median age at diagnosis is about 51 years, with the reported range extending down to 15 years, and the large majority of reported cases are women.

nodes.description: The amount of functional nuclear p27-Kip1 falls. In the upstream open reading frame mechanism this happens without any change in transcript level: both the wild-type and the mutant allele are transcribed in comparable amounts, and the deficit is in translation rather than in message. In most reported tumours the remaining wild-type allele is neither lost nor silenced at the transcript level, so the cell is left haploinsufficient rather than null.

nodes.description: p27-Kip1 is a potent inhibitor of cyclin E- and cyclin A-CDK2. Reduced nuclear p27 weakens that restraint and releases the G1 to S restriction point. This step is canonical p27 cell-cycle biology; it has not been measured directly in human MEN4 tumour tissue in any source retrieved, and is recorded here as the inferential link between the protein deficit and clonal expansion.

nodes.description: The minority route. In some MEN4 tumours loss of heterozygosity removes the retained wild-type allele, and loss of p27 staining has been seen in a parathyroid adenoma. This is the classical two-hit mechanism, and it is modelled here as a branch rather than as the trunk, because it is found in a minority of samples investigated while most tumours show reduced p27 with both alleles intact.

nodes.description: A four-base deletion in the conserved upstream open reading frame of the CDKN1B 5-prime untranslated region. It lengthens the upstream open reading frame peptide and shortens the intercistronic space, reducing reinitiation at the CDKN1B start codon and lowering p27 protein without reducing messenger RNA. Reported in a woman with acromegaly and a well-differentiated nonfunctioning pancreatic endocrine neoplasm whose tumour showed no loss of heterozygosity.
